title: Coalitional influence of majority for arbitrary coalitions
statement: Let $k,m:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and for each $q$ let $J_q$ be a set of coordinates among $k(q)+m(q)$ coordinates, with $|J_q|=k(q)$. Suppose $m(q)\to\infty$ and $k(q)/\sqrt{k(q)+m(q)}\to t\in\mathbb{R}$. For majority on the sign cube, the influence of $J_q$ toward either output, defined as the probability that the coalition can attain that output minus its probability under a uniformly random input, converges to $\tfrac12-Q(t)$, where $Q(t)=\Pr(Z>t)$ for a standard normal random variable $Z$.
hypotheses_covered: each $J_q$ is a subset of the $k(q)+m(q)$ coordinates
the coalition influence toward $+1$ converges to the stated limit
the coalition influence toward $-1$ converges to the stated limit
